internal.title: Incident Summary: Cart Service Elevated Error Rate Due to Error Injection Flag
internal.body:
At 12:31 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the cart service. Investigation identified that the elevated error rate (0.5) was caused by an error injection flag ('cartFailure') set to 50%, which injected errors related to 'Valkey connection error'. This was confirmed by logs and metrics. The flag was disabled at 12:51 UTC after approval, leading to immediate recovery and normalization of error rates.

No significant issues were found in the checkout service, which had a slightly elevated error rate but below alert thresholds and no latency or resource issues.

The incident was resolved by disabling the error injection flag, and service health was verified post-action.

external.body: Between 12:31 and 12:51 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced errors when adding items to their shopping cart. This was due to an internal testing configuration that inadvertently caused errors. The issue was identified and resolved promptly, and normal service has been restored. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

lessons.lesson: Ensure error injection flags are carefully controlled and monitored to prevent unintended impact on production services.

action_items: Review and improve controls around error injection flags to prevent accidental enabling in production.
Implement automated alerts for unusual flag changes that could impact service stability.
